label: Assam, Nagaland, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim and Tripura

items.heading: Assamese Fish Tenga
details: Key ingredients: fish, tomato, lemon or elephant apple, fenugreek seeds
Lightly fry fish pieces and set them aside.
Temper fenugreek seeds, then add tomato or a sour fruit like elephant apple.
Simmer until a light, sour broth forms.
Return the fish to the broth and simmer briefly before serving with rice.

items.heading: Til Pitha
details: Key ingredients: rice flour, sesame seeds, jaggery
Cook rice flour with water into a soft, pliable dough.
Prepare a sweet filling of roasted sesame seeds and jaggery.
Flatten the dough, add the filling and roll or fold it up.
Toast lightly on a griddle until fragrant.

items.heading: Axone Chutney
details: Key ingredients: fermented soybean (axone), dried chilies, ginger, garlic
Roast or lightly cook fermented soybean to mellow its sharpness.
Grind with dried chilies, ginger and garlic.
Adjust with salt to taste.
Serve as a pungent condiment alongside rice and meat.

items.heading: Bamboo Shoot Pork
details: Key ingredients: pork, fermented bamboo shoot, ginger, dried chili
Saute ginger and dried chili in a little oil until fragrant.
Add pork pieces and sear until lightly browned.
Add fermented bamboo shoot and a splash of water.
Simmer until the pork is tender and the flavors meld together.

items.heading: Apong Rice
details: Key ingredients: fermented rice, local herbs
Cook rice until well done, then spread out to cool slightly.
Mix with local herbs traditionally used for fermentation.
Allow the mixture to ferment for a day or two in a clean vessel.
Strain and serve as a mildly sweet, tangy traditional rice drink.

items.heading: Gundruk Soup
details: Key ingredients: fermented leafy greens, tomato, garlic
Saute garlic and tomato in a little oil until softened.
Add fermented leafy greens (gundruk) and a little water.
Simmer until the greens soften and the broth turns tangy.
Serve hot as a warming soup, especially in colder months.

items.heading: Berma Curry
details: Key ingredients: fermented fish (berma), vegetables, garlic
Saute garlic in a little oil until fragrant.
Add fermented fish and cook briefly to release its aroma.
Add chopped vegetables and a little water, simmering until tender.
Adjust seasoning and serve warm with rice.

items.heading: Chuak
details: Key ingredients: fermented rice, local herbs
Cook rice until well done, then cool slightly.
Mix with traditional herbs used for fermentation.
Allow the mixture to ferment for a day or two in a clean container.
Strain and serve as a mildly tangy traditional rice drink.
